definitions.explanation: A feeling of astonishment at something extraordinary, or something that inspires such astonishment. Emphasizes awe and admiration rather than fear.

examples.japanese: {驚異的|きょういてき}なスピードだ。
{自然|しぜん}の{驚異|きょうい}に{目|め}を{見張|みは}った。
examples.english: I marveled at the wonders of nature.

examples.japanese: {科学|かがく}の{進歩|しんぽ}は{人々|ひとびと}に{驚異|きょうい}と{希望|きぼう}を{与|あた}えてきた。
examples.english: Scientific progress has given people wonder and hope.

notes:
{驚異|きょうい} expresses a sense of wonder and astonishment at something extraordinary. The nuance is positive — awe and admiration rather than fear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {驚異的|きょういてき}な: astonishing, phenomenal (na-adjective form)
- {自然|しぜん}の{驚異|きょうい}: wonders of nature
- {驚異|きょうい}の{記録|きろく}: an astonishing record
- {驚異|きょうい}に{満|み}ちた: filled with wonder

WATCH OUT:
- {驚異|きょうい}: wonder, marvel (positive)
- {脅威|きょうい}: threat, menace (negative)
The kanji {驚|きょう} (surprise) vs. {脅|きょう} (threaten) distinguishes them.

REGISTER:
Somewhat formal and literary. In casual speech, すごい or {驚|おどろ}くべき are more common.
